newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RESEARCH - Portugal's ESR says Somague a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH - Portugal's ESR says Somague a buy.

text.p: Shares in construction company Somague SGPS are at a 35 percent discount to the overall Lisbon bourse and 20 percent to the construction sector in terms of price earnings (P/E), Espirito Santo Research said in a buy recommendation.
Somague was priced at 13 times 1997 earnings, on the basis of a share price of 1,700 escudos, and 11.6 times for 1998.
ESR, part of the Espirito Santo group, said that the purchase of construction concern Assiconstroi had opened up new perspectives for Somague.
"Somague has given proof that it has succeeded in overcoming the grave problems that faced it in the past," ESR said.
"In our opinion, these (share price) discounts to the market are no longer justified," it added.
It said it expected Somague to make a net profit of 1.87 billion escudos in 1997, up from 1.03 billion last year.
ESR said this represented almost a doubling of profit excluding the 250 million escudos of 'goodwill' included in the 1996 figure.
It said that in 1998 and 1999, the average annual growth in net profit should be 10 percent.
With the purchase of Assiconstroi, Somague became the largest construction company in Portugal with turnover seen at some 100 billion escudos this year. Its order book stood at some 130 billion.
Total debt after the purchase of Assiconstroi will be around 20 billion escudos, some 27 percent of liquid assets, ESR added.
